note: Algolia Search is a Search API backend (plugin id search_api_algolia). Real indexing needs external Algolia Application ID + Write API Key, so ALL medium/hard cases are grounded in LOCAL Drupal config only and never contact Algolia: the search_api_algolia.settings config object (debug/wait_for_delete, defaults false/false) and Search API Server entities using the search_api_algolia backend with dummy credentials (saving/deleting a Server does not connect to Algolia). Backend config keys: application_id, api_key, disable_truncate. Also provides processor algolia_item_splitter and drush search_api_algolia:delete (alias sapia-d). Server ids are namespaced sapia_*; scripts restore baseline (debug=false, wait_for_delete=false, no sapia_* servers).

evals.prompt: I want to index my Drupal 11 site's content into Algolia using search_api_algolia. What Search API backend do I choose, and what credentials must I provide on the server?
evals.expected_output: Add a Search API server with the 'Algolia' backend (plugin id search_api_algolia) and enter your Algolia Application ID (application_id) and Write API Key (api_key). Then create an index pointing at that server.

evals.prompt: Which module-level settings does search_api_algolia expose in its configuration object, and what do they do?
evals.expected_output: search_api_algolia.settings has 'debug' (verbose logging, default false) and 'wait_for_delete' (wait for Algolia delete operations to finish, default false).

evals.prompt: How do I flush queued Algolia object deletions from the command line with search_api_algolia, and what processor helps large items stay under Algolia's record-size limit?
evals.expected_output: Run drush search_api_algolia:delete (alias sapia-d, option --batch-size). The algolia_item_splitter Search API processor splits one item into multiple Algolia records to avoid the size limit.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the search_api_algolia configuration and state whether Algolia debug mode is currently enabled, and which setting controls it.
evals.expected_output: Debug mode is enabled: search_api_algolia.settings.debug is true.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a Search API server named sapia_known. Inspect it and report which Search API backend it uses and the Algolia Application ID configured on it.
evals.expected_output: The server sapia_known uses the search_api_algolia (Algolia) backend, with backend_config.application_id = APPID_KNOWN_123.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, turn on search_api_algolia's debug mode in its module settings. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: search_api_algolia.settings.debug is true (e.g. drush cset search_api_algolia.settings debug true).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a Search API server with machine name sapia_server that uses the Algolia backend (search_api_algolia), setting its Application ID to APPID_TASK and its Write API Key to KEY_TASK. Save it to the live site. (You do not need a real Algolia account for this.)
evals.expected_output: A search_api.server.sapia_server config entity exists with backend 'search_api_algolia' and backend_config.application_id = 'APPID_TASK' (api_key 'KEY_TASK').
